newsitem.title: CANADA: Fracmaster to rework 720 China oil wells.
newsitem.headline: Fracmaster to rework 720 China oil wells.

text.p: Canadian Fracmaster Ltd said on Thursday it won approval from the Chinese government to rehabilitate 720 oil wells in the country over 5 years.

Calgary-based Fracmaster, known for high-tech well stimulation techniques used extensively in Canada and Russia, said it planned to start operations with a 10-well program in the third quarter of this year and build up 140 wells in 1998.
Most of the workovers were expected to include "fraccing," or fracturing the rock at the bottom of wellbores to allow the oil to flow to the surface at higher rates.
Operations would also include re-entry and sidetrack drilling, Fracmaster said in its annual report.
"The company is optimistic that the initial work phase of a 10-well fraccing program will confirm the validity of current technical, operational and financial assumptions," Fracmaster said.
The wells are located in China's Shengli Petroleum Administration Bureau area, which produces about 220 million barrels of oil a year, or about 1/5 of the country's total output, Fracmaster said.
Fracmaster began its involvement in China in late 1994 when it performed 9 demonstration fractures to introduce its technology to the country's oil and gas industry.
That led to a production sharing agreement with the China National Oil and Gas Exploration and Development Corp, the company said. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
